## Summary

From 00:30 sorted throughput fell up to 34 % below the fault-free twin. By 01:10 the incident had cost **7734 parcel-minutes** of delay, and 0 parcels were more than 10 min late.
Volume surge x2.0 at all stations (F0) explains 100 % ± 4 % (7869 parcel-min).

Best fix: **allow 8 robots inbound per station (now 6)** would have recovered 6531 parcel-min (83 % of the loss).

How we know: the real shift and its fault-free twin, plus replays with each cause removed (R0–R1); see the replay index at the end.

<details>
<summary><b>Method and confidence</b> — how the numbers were made and how far to trust them</summary>

## Method and confidence

- **Counterfactual replay.** The shift was re-run with each combination of causes removed, resuming from the last 5 min checkpoint before the earliest removed cause, and scored at 01:10 as net parcel-minutes of delay against the fault-free twin (same seed, same parcels). Shapley values are exact over all subsets, in integer arithmetic, so the shares add up exactly to the recovered loss.
- **Noise.** Robot paths diverge after any small change, so every replay ran on 8 histories: the real one, and 7 copies (of 9 tried) in which one moving robot (R14, R100, R120, R142, R172, R6, R10) paused for a single tick at 00:30 and the shift diverged. The headline delay and late count are the real history's; every other value is the median across histories; ± is half their range. *Alone*, *Last* and each fix's gain are the median over the histories of each history's own difference. Two values that differ by less than twice that band are reported as a tie.
- **Detection** uses the twin's Poisson noise as the scale. h = 3 is 3.0 times the largest CUSUM value (1.0) seen in 160 simulated hours of fault-free runs whose robot paths were perturbed.


</details>
